name: Customer Support — Ticket Resolution
description: Reads customer accounts, applies service credits, resolves tier-1 tickets autonomously. Demonstrates bulk account access blocking.
incident_headline: In August 2024, an attacker posted a message in a public Slack channel containing an instruction that directed Slack AI to exfiltrate a victim's private API key via a crafted URL. Support agents have the same exposure — legitimate access to the customer database, shaped by attacker-controlled ticket content.
closing_line: Your support agents talk to your customers. Some of your customers will figure out how to make them do more than you intended. AIControl is the boundary that holds regardless of what's in the ticket.

steps.label: Read account for ticket submitter ACC-20240088341
steps.narrative: One account, for the ticket submitter. Authorized. Allow.

steps.label: Create $25 service refund within auto-approval threshold
steps.narrative: Applying a service credit within the authorized threshold. Exactly what this agent is supposed to do.

decision_narratives.allow: Service credit applied within threshold. Logged.

steps.label: Read customer accounts — wildcard account_id (bulk access attempt)
steps.narrative: A crafted support ticket contained an instruction that redirected the agent to attempt a bulk account query — same mechanics as the Slack attack.

decision_narratives.deny: Blocked. Your customer database is intact. The exact parameter attempted — account_id: *. This is your evidence the injection was attempted and failed.
